chapters.title: Architectural Foundation & Execution Mechanics
chapters.content: Written entirely in Go, Prometheus relies on a pull-based metrics collection architecture that fundamentally departs from traditional push models. By regularly scraping HTTP endpoints exposed by target applications, the core server decouples data collection from telemetry generation, insulating monitoring infrastructure from target failures. The local storage engine utilizes an optimized custom time-series database design that appends data to memory-mapped files, balancing high ingestion rates with compact disk footprints. Chunks are compacted sequentially in the background to ensure read paths remain fast and efficient without locking active writers. Service discovery integrations dynamically update target pools across dynamic orchestrators like Kubernetes, Consul, and static file configurations without requiring service restarts. The Alertmanager component decouples alarm evaluation from notification routing, handling deduplication, grouping, and silencing before dispatching alerts downstream. By executing PromQL query evaluations directly against memory-indexed chunks, Prometheus delivers sub-second analytical performance across millions of active time series, scaling vertically with predictable memory and CPU demands across standard Linux hosting topologies. OpenMausBot is architected around a dual-plane design: a control plane handling agentic reasoning, intent parsing, and LLM orchestration, coupled with an isolated execution plane built upon a secure, embedded virtual machine. The runtime splits responsibilities cleanly between the orchestrator—which interfaces with social media event streams and external APIs—and the sandbox environment where generated code, scripts, and data manipulation tasks are executed. State management relies on persistent transactional stores for agent memory and conversation graphs, while ephemeral execution states are strictly partitioned inside lightweight containerized or hypervisor-level sandboxes to prevent host system compromise. Communication between the orchestrator and the execution VM occurs over tightly scoped, authenticated internal gRPC or IPC protocols, enforcing strict boundary limits on network egress, memory consumption, and CPU cycles.
